Hadhrat Ali (RA) Rebukes a Man for Regarding him to be Superior to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Katheer narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "You are the best of people." "Have you seen Rasulullaah ﷺ?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) enquired. When the man replied that he had not, Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked further, "Have you then seen Abu Bakr (RA)?" "No," came the reply. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then said, "Take note of this! Had you mentioned that you had seen Rasulullaah ﷺ, I would have had you executed and had you mentioned that you had seen Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA), I would have had you lashed (for slander)."[^2]

Hadhrat Alqamah reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once delivered a lecture to them. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "The news has reached me that some people regard me to be superior to Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA). Had I warned against this previously, I would have certainly given punishment for it. However, I dislike meting punishment for something I have not warned against. Now after this proclamation of mine if anyone says anything like this, he will be regarded as a slanderer and shall so be punished as one. The best of all people after Rasulullaah ﷺ is Abu Bakr (RA) and then Umar (RA). Thereafter, when they had departed we started many new things concerning which Allaah shall decide as He pleases (whether they were correct or not)."[^3]
A Historic Lecture of Hadhrat Ali (RA) Concerning the Superiority of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Suwayd bin Ghaflah narrates that he once passed by a group of people who were degrading the status of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA). When he reported this to Hadhrat Ali (RA), he said, "May Allaah curse those who harbour anything besides good towards the two illustrious men. They were the brothers and extremely close companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then mounted the pulpit and delivered an eloquent lecture in which he said:
"What is the matter with some people who speak about the two leaders of the Quraysh and the two fathers of the Muslims in a manner that I would never. I absolve myself from what they say and shall punish for it. I swear by the Being Who splits the seed and Who creates the soul that it is only the Allaah-fearing
Ishaari and La'alkaa'i, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.447).
Ibn Aasim, Ibn Shaaheen, La'alkaa'i, Isbahaani and Ibn Asaakir.
